$comment: The accessibility RATCHET, and the reason it exists.
axe was pointed at real pages for the first time on 2026-08-04. Counts are frozen per
(surface, state, project): a RISE fails, a fall is re-frozen (ADR-928).
2026-08-17 -- A BARE INTEGER IS NOW A READING, AND EQUALITY IS HOW IT IS CHECKED
Until today every number in this file was compared with `total <= allowed`, so every one of
them was a CEILING whatever the prose said about it. That is the weaker claim, and its cost
is exact: every unit of headroom under a ceiling is a place a real regression can sit while
CI prints a tick. The three shell entries below were the extreme case -- 12, 7 and 8 seeded
as RAW pre-waiver totals whose true residual was believed to be 0-3 -- but the same hole was
open, smaller, under all 49.
So the default flipped (ADR-1058). A bare integer is a READING: the value measured here IS
this number, and test/e2e/a11y-ratchet.ts asserts EQUALITY against it. A regression fails,
and so does an IMPROVEMENT -- because a file that has stopped describing the product is the
failure mode that let /spaces sit at a stale 44, and an annotation nobody reads in a green
run is not a record. Re-recording is one command, so failing on good news costs a re-run.
A ceiling is still available where a number genuinely cannot be asserted, but it is now an
EXCEPTION WITH PAPERWORK: an object carrying `ceiling`, `why` (what is missing before it can
become a reading), `retiredBy` (the command that replaces it), and the same `frozen` +
`history` provenance scripts/adoption-baselines.json has demanded since 2026-08-04.
`pnpm check:a11y-baselines` enforces that statically, with no browser, on every PR:
frozen.value must equal ceiling, history must chain, and a declared direction must match the
arithmetic -- so a raise cannot be filed as a re-freeze and a number cannot move at all
without a written reason in the same diff. It also prints every live ceiling on every run.
The three below stay ceilings, and NOT because a ceiling is right for them -- because
converting them honestly needs an axe run against a deployment with the beta storage state
(backlog OWN-002), and inventing the number instead would be a fabricated baseline, which is
strictly worse than an honest ceiling. Retire them the moment a real capture lands.
STATE (re-derived from this file 2026-08-13): 49 contexts, 187 serious+ elements, 18 clean.
The line below is kept because its -63 explanation is still true of /pricing; the 40/156/15
it quoted was the 2026-08-04 capture and had drifted as surfaces were added. Re-derive rather
than trust a prose count: sum the integers in this file.
Superseded: 40 contexts, 156 serious+ elements, 15 clean. Down from 219 -- all of
that -63 was /pricing, whose value ledger rendered 21 `text-success` cells on the canvas
band at 4.05:1 instead of on white at 4.67:1.
WHY /spaces (44) AND /the-community (39) ARE NOW STALE, NOT ACCURATE:
ADR-929 gave accentize() a band argument and fixed all 32 call sites, which is the defect
these two numbers were measuring. They have NOT been re-captured against a deployment, so
they read high. A fall cannot fail CI, so this is stale-but-safe. Re-capture to correct it.
COVERAGE, and the correction that got the CAUSE wrong (2026-08-04):
An earlier header said '44 of 84 tests do not run without PW_STORAGE_STATE'. The 44 was
right and the cause was wrong. The real split was 27 mobile-project contrast skips that
are DELIBERATE (a11y.spec.ts:244 -- contrast is viewport-independent, so the desktop
project carries the render-state sweep), 12 genuinely blocked on the beta storage state,
and 5 for /circles.
The /circles five are now GONE rather than skipping: it sat in EDITABLE_PAGES (so the
registry offered it to anonymous visitors) and in proxy.ts PROTECTED_PATHS (so anon was
redirected to /sign-in). publicSurfaces() now filters the registry against the proxy's own
list, so a page that anon cannot reach is not an anon surface. That retired 5 a11y contexts
and 8 visual tests that could never have produced a number. Open /circles to visitors and
they come back automatically, with no edit to the test harness.
So the honest coverage line is now: 12 tests owner-gated on a seeded beta account, 27
deliberate, everything else measuring.
THIS NUMBER IS A FLOOR, NOT A CENSUS. axe returns INCOMPLETE rather than violation for any
element over a background-image, under a pseudo-element covering >25%, or at opacity 0. So
every ink band's contrast debt is unmeasured, as is everything below the fold in a Reveal.
Every number here is debt with a date on it. Lower them; never raise them.
Re-freeze with: PW_A11Y_UPDATE=1 pnpm test:e2e:a11y && pnpm a11y:baselines
Check the FILE (no browser needed) with: pnpm check:a11y-baselines
2026-08-11 -- WHAT THESE NUMBERS NOW COUNT, AND THE NINE THAT WERE JUST SEEDED
A number here no longer counts every serious+ element axe finds. It counts every one
NOBODY HAS DECIDED ABOUT. Elements matching a named entry in test/e2e/a11y-waivers.ts
are subtracted first and printed as `a11y-waived` annotations instead. See ADR-985.
That change is why the marketing numbers below did NOT move even though run 31453092474
reported 15 marketing contexts over their baselines. Every one of those rises was the
owner's 2026-08-06 palette decision (white label on the brand amber) reaching axe for the
first time. Raising 15 counts to absorb one decision is exactly what ADR-980 forbids: the
raised number would also permit any unrelated serious violation up to it, forever. The
decision got named instead, and the counts stayed frozen.
THE NINE NEW KEYS ARE A FIRST FLOOR, NOT AN ABSORBED REGRESSION (FINALIZE 1.3).
/feed, /settings and /spaces/<slug>/manage had NO key at all until now, so they fell to
$defaultMax (0) and failed all nine of their checks the first time PW_SPACE_SLUG let them
be photographed. Establishing a floor for a surface that has never been measured is a
capture; re-freezing a surface that got worse is erasure. These are the first kind.
Per context, and what is actually in each number:
/feed [dawn-dark, contrast only, desktop]        0  measured 3, ALL three the amber. Clean.
/feed [dawn-light, desktop]                     12  CEILING, not a reading -- see below.
/feed [dawn-light, mobile]                       2  measured 6: 4 amber/success (waived) +
2 target-size, both now FIXED. Expect 0.
/settings [dawn-dark, contrast only, desktop]    0  measured 1, the amber. Clean.
/settings [dawn-light, desktop]                  7  CEILING, not a reading -- see below.
/settings [dawn-light, mobile]                   1  measured 1: the .sm:hidden search button,
now FIXED. Expect 0.
/spaces/danieltyack/manage [dawn-dark, ...]      0  measured 2, both the amber. Clean.
/spaces/danieltyack/manage [dawn-light, desktop] 8  CEILING, not a reading -- see below.
/spaces/danieltyack/manage [dawn-light, mobile]  1  measured 2: 1 amber (waived) + the same
.sm:hidden button, now FIXED. Expect 0.
THE THREE 'CEILING' ENTRIES ARE THE WEAKEST NUMBERS IN THIS FILE, deliberately and
temporarily. They are the raw measured totals, seeded WITHOUT subtracting waivers, because
the run log printed only the first 5 nodes of each violation and these three had 11, 7 and 8.
Every node that WAS visible on all three was an accepted palette pair, so the true post-waiver
residual is very likely 0-3, not 12/7/8. A ceiling was chosen over a guess: a guess that is
too low turns CI red for a reason nobody can reproduce. The node cap in a11y.spec.ts is now 40
rather than 5, so the NEXT run prints every element and reports the real number as an
`a11y-improved` annotation. Tighten these three the moment it does; until then they are the
widest holes in this gate.
(2026-08-17: those three are now DECLARED ceilings rather than bare integers that happened to
be compared loosely -- same numbers, same reasons, but each one now carries its `why` and its
provenance inline, `pnpm check:a11y-baselines` refuses to let any of them move without a
written reason, and every other number in this file became a reading checked with equality.
A capture that measures one of them replaces the whole object with a bare integer.)
NOT WAIVED, and staying failed on purpose: amber used as DISPLAY TEXT (`.text-primary`
headlines, 2.18-2.86:1 against a 3:1 bar) and the `.text-text/10` watermark numerals in the
dark skins (1.3:1). The owner's decision covers a white label on an amber FILL. It does not
cover the amber as ink, and the waiver list is written so it cannot be stretched to.
2026-08-11 -- WHY /discover WENT RED, AND THE ONE SENTENCE ABOVE THAT WAS WRONG
The paragraph above used to end '...and the tinted chips on /discover'. That grouped two
unlike things under one justification, and it is what turned pr-compare red the first run
it was a required context: /discover came in 1 over baseline in three contexts.
The amber-as-ink half of that sentence is right and stands. The chip half was not. The two
`bg-warning-bg text-warning` chips on the CircleCards are not the owner's palette decision at
all -- they are --color-warning on --color-warning-bg, which check-contrast.mjs ALREADY holds
at a frozen floor of 3.32 in every light state. Its sibling, the success chip, was admitted to
the waiver list on exactly that citation. The warning chip -- the weaker of the two -- was
excluded by a sentence about a decision that does not govern it. Two identical things, two
different rules.
The test that mattered: does waiving it let anything escape? No. The pair is already ratcheted
in the instrument that owns token pairs, and check:contrast fails loudly if it worsens. Counting
it here a second time bought no accountability -- it was the same debt under a different name,
which is the exact duplication ADR-985 built this mechanism to end.
Also seeded: the two emboss composites the SMALL button paints (#c07b28 and #b97124). Four
emboss entries were frozen off the large CTA; a shorter label at 14.875px shifts the blur
weighting, so axe rounds the composite to a neighbouring hex. Same button family, same finish,
same owner decision, one more measurement.
Net: -2 chips and -1 emboss per /discover context. 6 -> 3 against a baseline of 5, 5 -> 2
against 4, twice. The amber display headlines are still counted, inside those numbers, as the
undecided debt they are. NOTHING WAS RE-BASELINED to get this green.

/ [midnight-dark, contrast only, desktop.why: Not a reading, and not a run-to-run wobble: a REAL, MEASURED contrast regression the owner has chosen to carry rather than fix today (2026-08-18). The failing pair is white text on the amber button, #FFFFFF on #F0AD4E = 1.95:1 against a 4.5:1 requirement. It is PRE-EXISTING and was invisible until LIVE-008 fixed a selector that could never match, so midnight-dark now paints its real palette instead of falling back to the generic .dark one. Two remedies are measured and recorded on backlog row OWN-014: darken the foreground on the amber (#1C2535 on #F0AD4E = 7.90:1, brand colour untouched) or give midnight-dark a genuine primary-strong (#7A4A0E with white = 7.46:1, the shape midnight-LIGHT already uses at #8C5410 = 6.19:1). Note the remedy OWN-014 originally proposed is a NO-OP here: midnight-dark sets --color-primary-strong to #F0AD4E, the same value as --color-primary, so swapping to it changes nothing. This is a ceiling and not a reading because the number is expected to go to 0, not to hold.
